items.stem: According to the opening strophe, what does the nightingale do from a bower among the ivy?
options: Trilleth her ceaseless song
Warns the city of a Theban raid
Leads the worn stranger back to the road
Keeps silent until a king has spoken

items.stem: What is Colonus called in line 695?
options: A steed-famed land
A land of plague and famine
A barren rock without a stream
A city already wasted by war

items.stem: Complete the line: “The starred _____ shine,”
options: olives
thistles
narcissi
cedars

items.stem: Complete the line: “And here there grows, _____, untamed,”
options: withered
planted
gilded
unpruned

items.stem: What gifts does the chorus say it owes to Poseidon?
options: Horsemanship and seafaring, which the ode credits to him
A new Theban throne prepared for the worn stranger alone
The laurel crown reserved for the Delphic god Apollo now
The power to call a wasting plague down on any named foe

items.stem: In the opening lines, how is the visitor described?
options: A worn stranger who has come here for rest
A king returning home in a public triumph
A herald sent in haste from Theban Creon now
A god walking the sacred grove in human disguise

items.stem: What does the olive stand for when the ode calls it a “Terror to foemen’s spear”?
options: It presents the tree as a living defence of the city
It claims the sacred tree is cut to make enemy spears
It says the city's foes come just to harvest the fruit
It warns that the holy grove will be felled in a siege

items.stem: What tree does the ode celebrate?
options: The olive
The oak
The laurel
The cypress

items.stem: What is the tone of the ode?
options: Proud and loving
Fearful and uncertain
Angry at the worn stranger
Mocking of the city's gods

items.stem: Complete the line: “That feed _____’ stream,”
options: Ismenus
Cephisus
Eurotas
Ilissus

items.stem: Complete the line: “By Pelops’ Dorian isle _____,”
options: forgotten
hidden
ruined
unclaimed

items.stem: What do the sleepless fountains do for the land, according to the ode?
options: They keep the soil fertile without ceasing
They dry the fields so the olive can grow
They wash the stranger's past from memory
They mark a hard border with the Theban plain

items.stem: Who is “the Cyprian queen of the golden rein” in this ode?
options: Aphrodite, who also visits this favoured plain
Hera, queen of the Argive sky and marriage
Artemis, huntress of the sunless windless glade
Athena, already praised as the city's own defender

items.stem: What does the claim that the tree is unnamed in Asian soil and not claimed by Pelops’ Dorian isle emphasize?
options: It treats the olive as uniquely Attic, not Asian or Dorian
The chorus admits the tree was first grown in Asian gardens
The olive, in this song, belongs equally to every Greek city
The tree will soon be sent abroad as a gift from Athens

items.stem: Who defends the olive, according to the ode?
options: The Grey-eyed Goddess (Athena)
Zeus alone, without any care from Athena
Apollo, speaking from the Delphic hearth
Creon, acting as guardian of Theban land

items.stem: Complete the line: “Nor youth nor _____ age destroys”
options: happy
distant
sudden
withering

items.stem: Complete the line: “Son of _____, our king divine,”
options: Helios
Ares
Kronos
Hermes

items.stem: What does “Self-nurtured year by year” make the olive stand for?
options: It renews itself in this soil without being imported or forced
The city's boys must replant the same tree again each spring
The tree was brought from Asia in this very same generation
Theseus planted it on the very day he welcomed the stranger

items.stem: In this ode, the Mother and Daughter for whom a crocus wreath is twined are:
options: Demeter and Persephone
Athena and her companion Artemis
Antigone and Ismene, the stranger's daughters
The nymphs who fostered the Bacchic child

items.stem: What contrast does the ode draw when it says that neither youth nor age destroys the plant?
options: The tree outlasts the span of a human life
The tree lives only while the city's boys are young
Old age is about to bring the grove down
The stranger's youth will be restored by the fruit

items.stem: Complete the line: “And the Muses’ _____ will never disdain”
options: armor
harvest
quire
temple

items.stem: Complete the line: “Swift as the _____’ hundred feet”
options: Furies
Harpies
Nereids
Gorgons

items.stem: What does the phrase “heaven-favoured plain” add to the visit of the Muses?
options: It presents the place as chosen and honoured by the gods
It means the favoured plain is empty of every mortal voice
It claims Colonus has already taken the old place of Delphi
It warns that the gods are now about to leave the whole land

items.stem: What does the pairing of the tree's wild growth with its feeding of the city's boys make the olive stand for?
options: The tree's strength is native and wild, yet it still nourishes the city
The chorus wants the sacred grove cut back and formally trained
The olive is treated as too wild to be of any civic use at all
A king must first tame the wild tree before it can feed anyone

items.stem: How does the yearly, self-nurtured life of the olive work in that stanza?
options: It stresses a continuous, native life that no other land is said to claim
It means the city's boys must plant a new tree every single year
It admits the sacred tree was imported from the Dorian isle
It refers to the nightingale's yearly return in early spring

items.stem: What is the effect of repeating “The might of the horse, the might of the sea”?
options: The repeated word might balances two powers as one boast of the land
The chorus shows it cannot decide which of the gifts matters more now
The line reduces Poseidon to being no more than a god of horses
The stanza prepares a confession that Athens has no real sea fleet
